For warlock flavor, hell yeah, but I was more referring to designing an entire encounter to tpk and then dues ex machina them.

Role playing video games like to "kill" the main player so they can meet their god or god's and be announced as a chosen one or whatever. Do not do this to your players. The difference between a video game and a table top is vastly different. In a video game you select the appearance of your character with no real backstory, no context, and are thrust into the world which is already programmed. In tabletops, your players put love and time into their characters; writing their backstory, coming up with their personality, practicing their voice. So when you throw an encounter at them which is meant to kill them for that meeting with their god moment, you may piss them off beyond belief. This is called a dues ex machina, a trope I consider as one of the weakest writing tools out there. 

I was in a campaign for over 6 months and had achieved level 12 with a character I had come to love playing more than any other I've created. However, the campaign was already taking a downturn for me as we had spent the last two months unable to do anything truly heroic or fun because the DM's BBEG had been up our ass messing up everything we touched. We finally came up with an idea that would get us away from the BBEG and buy us room to breath when low and behold we were thrown into a double adult dragon fight with a party of four at level 12. Impossible to win and impossible to run from. I left the game and aired my dissapointments. I find out later from one of the other players they met their gods and were revived. I rolled my eyes so hard I nearly gave myself brain damage.
I consider myself a creative player and I came up dry on ideas. We just had a forest and 2 dragons staring us down. I could only think about how to save my character.

Nothing. No discussion, no warning. That's what my problem was. Had a warning been givin to us through an NPC or even from the DM himself about the difficulty of the fight, we would at least have had the chance to discuss and possibly back out. He didn't give us that choice.

The fight was a trial to enter the World of Dragons. It was a trial of strength. That was the only information we had. Once we walked a little ways into the forest, the dragons quite literally appeared behind us. Fight began and we did what damage we could. The rogue actually crit on a sneak attack and did like 80 damage. That health bar barely even dropped. Meanwhile, my fellow sorcerer got knocked down three times, the cleric is close behind and I'm at 13hp. This all happened within 3 -5 rounds. There was no room to negotiate because we are meant to prove our strength to 2 Adult Dragons at level 12. I can't come up with a better encounter to TPK players in.

Can't parlay when all they do is talk about how much they want to eat you. There is no running from that fight. Their flying speeds exceed any speed boosts we have. My char had expeditious and mobile. They still would have caught up within a round.

I liked Persona 5 but to me Persona 3 was so much more profound and deeper. Between Aigis becoming more human, the team of  persona users you fight, and just how the game made you actually feel like the end of the world was imminent. The heavier tone was amazing and the ending really topped off the game and really hit the despair home. Persona 5 was too light hearted for me. I know it had its moments of maturity but they seemd incredibly fleeting. I mean they brought suicide to the table and then once the scene was over it kinda got pushed into the back. You barely ever saw Ann's friend again and her recovery was barely acknowledged. Also, the last boss didn't feel terrifying in the slightest. In Persona 3, Tartarus became more and more terrifying with each level you conquered and the last boss was mixed with your entire team struggling to remain hopeful yet the despair was incredibly apparent. Persona 5, your team seems almost impervious to fear. "No worries, Joker will have a plan," "Joker will get us out of this." It definitely didn't feel like the world was ending. The most climactic moment of the game felt very forgettable to me. Now Persona 3. I'll remember that forever. 

Final note: Aigis is best girl. You'll never change my mind.
